roleTitle: Embedded Software Engineer, Charging Station Firmware
jobDescription: The company operates a network of public vehicle charging stations, and their firmware is the software this engineer ships to the field. The role covers the release of firmware to the installed station fleet over the air, the field on-call for station faults raised by the operations centre, the watch on charging session success rates after each release, the hardware-in-the-loop test rig before release, and the release notes with each version's known limitations. Reports to the head of station software; works with the operations centre, the hardware team and the field technicians.
requirements: Has released firmware to the installed station fleet over the air and watched charging session success rates after each release.
Takes the field on-call for faults the operations centre raises against stations and has handled fleet-wide incidents.
Coordinates each release's station rollout waves with the operations centre and records own responsibility boundaries.
Tests each firmware version on the hardware-in-the-loop rig before release with a documented test record.
Writes the release notes with each version's known limitations and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Released fourteen firmware versions over the air to the installed fleet of about 3,200 public charging stations between 2022 and 2025, each in rollout waves agreed with the operations centre and each under a release ticket in my name.

Watched the charging session success rate on the fleet dashboard after each release wave and held the field on-call for the station faults the operations centre raised; the fleet-wide fault of October 2023, when a connector firmware bug stopped sessions on one station model, was handled on my on-call shift and is recorded in the operations incident log.
Coordinated the rollout waves for each release with the operations centre, recording in the release ticket which checks were mine and which belonged to the operations centre's wave sign-off.
Tested each firmware version on the hardware-in-the-loop rig before release, with the rig test record attached to the release ticket.
Wrote the release notes for each version, listing the known limitations on the older station models and the hand-over conditions for the field technicians.
Work sample: the release tickets for the last five versions with their rig test records and wave plans, and the operations incident log record for the October 2023 fleet-wide fault.

Recruiter screen: the candidate described the release waves, the on-call shift pattern and the October 2023 fault, naming the affected station model; the account agrees with the resume and the incident record.

Hiring manager pre-read: the head of station software asks that the packet cite the release tickets and the incident record, and keep the rig testing separate from the field releases when listing requirements.
